question: What is the main goal of decontaminating medical tools in the ward?

options.B: To remove or destroy harmful germs
options.C: To make the tools look shiny and clean
options.D: To save money on buying new equipment

explanation: Decontamination is all about getting rid of germs on instruments so we don't pass infections to our patients and colleagues. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: A nurse forgets to wipe down a stethoscope between seeing patients. What is the biggest risk here?

options.A: Spreading hospital-acquired infections to other patients
options.C: Ruining the rubber tubing of the stethoscope
options.D: Making the metal part rust instantly

explanation: Stethoscopes touch many patients back-to-back. If we don't clean them, they easily carry germs from one bed to the next! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which cleaning process is strong enough to kill even tough bacterial spores?
explanation: Only true sterilization wipes out all forms of life, including stubborn bacterial spores that resist regular cleaning. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why must you always wash instruments before disinfecting or sterilizing them?

options.A: Dried blood or dirt hides germs from disinfectants
options.B: Water helps surgical steel conduct electricity
options.C: Soap adds helpful weight to the tools

explanation: Think of dried blood or body fluids like a shield protecting the germs underneath. If you don't wash it off first, the disinfectant can't reach them! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: According to Spaulding's rules, which items need high-level disinfection?
explanation: Semi-critical items touch mucous membranes (like respiratory equipment), so they need high-level disinfection to knock out almost all germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: You are getting a surgical scalpel ready for an operation. How should it be processed?

options.A: Low-level disinfection since it only touches skin
options.B: High-level disinfection because it has a sharp blade
options.C: Just washing since it is stainless steel
options.D: Sterilization because it cuts into sterile tissue

explanation: Because scalpels go right inside sterile body tissues, they are 'critical items' and must go through full sterilization to keep the patient safe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the very first thing you should do with an instrument right after using it?

options.A: Put it straight into the autoclave
options.B: Soak it in pure bleach for a full day
options.C: Leave it on the tray to air dry
options.D: Remove heavy dirt at the point of use

explanation: Always wipe off gross soil right away! Waiting lets blood and tissue dry up, making them ten times harder to clean later. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why do instruments need to be completely dry before going into the autoclave for sterilization?

options.A: To keep the metal magnetic while stored
options.B: To stop moisture from blocking the steam or diluting chemicals
options.C: To keep the instruments lightweight for technicians
options.D: To prevent the washing machine from sparking

explanation: Extra water can get in the way of the steam doing its job, or weaken the packaging. Keeping things dry ensures proper sterilization! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: What happens if a disinfectant surface dries up before its required contact time is finished?

options.A: The chemical turns into safe powder
options.B: The process actually happens much faster
options.D: The disinfection fails and needs to be restarted

explanation: Disinfectants need time to work! If the surface dries too fast, the germs might survive, so keep it wet for the recommended time. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why do nurses need to mix a fresh batch of chlorine cleaning solution every day?

options.A: Fresh mixes smell nice and keep patients calm
options.B: Unused mixtures turn hard and block spray bottles
options.C: Old solutions will permanently stain hospital tiles
options.D: Chlorine loses its strength and power over time

explanation: Chlorine is quite unstable and weakens quickly. Yesterday's mix might look okay, but it won't have enough germ-killing power left! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: What personal protective gear is a must-have when handling strong chemical disinfectants and dirty instruments?

options.A: Open-toed sandals to keep feet cool
options.B: A clean white cotton nursing uniform
options.C: Heavy-duty utility gloves and eye protection

explanation: Harsh chemicals and dirty splashes can hurt your skin and eyes. Always protect yourself with utility gloves and goggles! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why is an emergency eyewash station placed right next to where chemicals are mixed?

options.A: To give nurses clean water to wash hands
options.B: To quickly flush out eyes if chemical splashes happen
options.C: To provide running water for soaking instruments
options.D: To test the water pressure in the ward daily

explanation: Accidents happen fast when pouring chemicals. Having an eyewash station right there means you can flush your eyes immediately and prevent serious damage. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Where should used syringe needles and surgical blades go immediately after you use them?

options.A: In a black general waste bin
options.D: In an open plastic wash basin

explanation: Sharps go straight into the safety box (sharps container) right at the bedside to prevent accidental needle-sticks for you and your team. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why should you never wipe up a fresh blood spill with a dry cloth first?

options.A: It sends infectious droplets into the air you breathe
options.B: It makes the blood turn into an permanent stain
options.C: It makes the cloth stick tightly to the floor
options.D: It ruins the fibers of the cleaning cloth

explanation: Wiping wet blood with a dry cloth acts like a sprayer, launching tiny infectious particles right into the air for people nearby to inhale. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)
